video_title: Mikal Bridges' Future With the Knicks | Eastern Conference Check-In

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's recent performance and the Knicks' loss to Charlotte
quotes.excerpt: Grayson Allen outscored the combination of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden by five points.
quotes.quote: If you look at his numbers for this season, he had only gone over 19 points once. In his two games coming in, I think it was 18 points total, including 11 the other night against Charlotte. In fact, he and Donovan Mitchell both had 11 in that brutal loss to Charlotte. Grayson Allen had 27. Grayson Allen outscored the combination of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden by five points. I was really worried about the Cavaliers and where this was headed. I give them credit because if they played the Knicks in a playoff series, the Knicks are going to beat them. But I felt like Cleveland was desperate for a win. I didn't think that James Harden had it in him, but give him credit, that was his best game of the season.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on the Cavs loss to Charlotte: Grayson Allen outscored the combination of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden by five points. It was a brutal loss for Cleveland.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' strategy regarding Mikal Bridges' future and playing time
quotes.excerpt: I think they are clearly trying to move him and I think what happens too is notice who's coming in for him.
quotes.quote: He makes a lot and the Knicks got a lot to get him, but I think they are clearly trying to move him and I think what happens too is notice who's coming in for him. They are going with another guard and really what they do, it takes pressure off of Jalen Brunson because then he can play off the ball a little bit more. And then he can become more of a scoring guard. So Mikal's minutes going down helps Jalen. But I got to say this in defense of Mikal Bridges, and I didn't think he played well when he was on the Brooklyn Nets. He didn't look happy. They needed him to be more of a number one or a number two guy and he wasn't comfortable in that role.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on Mikal Bridges: The Knicks are clearly trying to move him. His minutes going down helps Jalen Brunson play off the ball more, but Bridges never looked comfortable in that number one or two scoring role.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: Mikal Bridges' performance in the playoffs compared to regular season
quotes.excerpt: But to the guy's credit, in the playoffs he's elevated his play, which is the mark of a good player.
quotes.quote: If you look at his first two years with the Knicks, his regular seasons have not been good. But to the guy's credit, in the playoffs he's elevated his play, which is the mark of a good player. I go all the way back to when like Allen Houston was on the Knicks and every year in the playoffs his scoring average went up. So even though it might have been up and down during the regular season, you knew you could count on him come playoff time. I'm sure it frustrates Mike Brown and it probably frustrates some of Bridges' teammates, but he does have a track record. He was great against Jason Tatum a couple years ago in the playoffs. Last year he had some really good moments as well.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola notes that while Mikal Bridges has struggled in the regular season with the Knicks, he has a track record of elevating his play in the playoffs when it counts.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential trade return for Mikal Bridges and salary cap implications
quotes.excerpt: You are probably trying to trade him to a team that could take on a lot of his salary.
quotes.quote: You are probably trying to trade him to a team that could take on a lot of his salary, so it's not like you are taking matching salaries back. And I'm sure they would try to get a pick out of that as well. What did they give up? Five first-round picks? They are not going to get that. You look at the going price on a lot of these players. Look what the Celtics got for Jaylen Brown. They got a serviceable player in Paul George, but he's up there in age and I think what you get back, one first-round pick and maybe the right to swap.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on a potential Mikal Bridges trade: The Knicks are not going to get back the five first-round picks they gave up. You look at the market, you are likely looking at one first-round pick and maybe a swap.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential fit and impact on the Knicks' roster
quotes.excerpt: I think that he would have looked at it as, all right, I'm at a stage of my career where I'm a role player.
quotes.quote: I think when you have LeBron, there's a lot that comes with it because he's this huge celebrity. He's got a lot of people with him. But I also think he would have looked at it as, all right, I'm at a stage of my career where I'm a role player. I'm a high-level role player. I could do a lot of different things. I could facilitate. I think in the fourth quarter of close games, that's still a guy that you would want out there. He can now guard power forwards and centers. And more importantly too, if you had signed LeBron, he's not on Philadelphia. Philadelphia does not have the record they have if LeBron's on that team.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on the hypothetical of LeBron James on the Knicks: He would be a high-level role player at this stage of his career, but his presence alone would change the trajectory of teams like Philadelphia.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's leadership and performance in the Celtics' recent games
quotes.excerpt: I really am the guy on the team, because I thought Tatum handled it really well.
quotes.quote: It changes Tatum's thinking into, I really am the guy on the team, because I thought Tatum handled it really well. Jaylen Brown was the one that was creating this whole rivalry and how we have beef, the lamb chops and gravy thing. And Tatum's got the perception as he's the quiet one, he's a little soft. But Tatum went over to at least slap Jaylen Brown's hand. Jaylen Brown is spitting the ball because he's trying to ignore Tatum. I thought it was really weak on Jaylen Brown's part. And what does Tatum do? He goes out and has a great game. And you knew that they were that LeBron was going to try to do everything he can to support Jaylen Brown have a big game. Jaylen Brown finishes with 13. The guy that he's traded for finishes with 36. He almost scores three times as many points as Jaylen Brown.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola calls Jaylen Brown ignoring Jayson Tatum weak: Tatum went to slap his hand but Brown was trying to ignore him. Then Tatum goes out and drops 36 while Brown finishes with 13. The guy he was traded for outplayed him.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: The Celtics' decision to trade Jaylen Brown and market value
quotes.excerpt: Brad Stevens knows straight up, you are not getting the better player in return just from an age standpoint.
quotes.quote: First of all, Brad Stevens is not dumb. So Brad Stevens knows straight up, you are not getting the better player in return just from an age standpoint. Right now the contracts are the same. It's that Jaylen Brown has a longer-term contract, then eventually he was going to ask for an extension. So I think that they got rid of him probably a year too early as opposed to a year too late. But I think it also tells you what was the market like for Jaylen Brown. I think they could have had Giannis maybe if they had thrown in another player or two, but I don't think Boston wanted to go there. So Brad Stevens knew that when he made that trade, what the reaction was going to be.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on the Jaylen Brown trade: Brad Stevens knew he was not getting the better player back, but he got rid of him a year too early rather than a year too late given the contract situation.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: Zion Williamson's lack of playoff experience since being drafted
quotes.excerpt: He was a number one overall pick in 2019. He's yet to play in a playoff game.
quotes.quote: I watched Zion Williamson last night. He was a number one overall pick in 2019. He's yet to play in a playoff game. Much less win a round, go to a conference finals, get to a finals, win a championship. You know, when you're drafting guys high like the Celtics did with Jason Tatum and Jaylen Brown, and if you said, you'll get like 130 playoff games between the two of them, you'll go to two finals, you'll win a championship, every team would say, where do I sign up for that?
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on Zion Williamson: He was a number one overall pick in 2019 and has yet to play in a single playoff game. It is a stark contrast to the success of Tatum and Brown in Boston.

quotes.speaker: Frank Isola
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's longevity and commitment to competition
quotes.excerpt: There's a reason why Tom Brady played as long as he did with Tampa.
quotes.quote: There's a reason why Tom Brady played as long as he did with Tampa. There's a reason why LeBron is still playing at the age he's at. Kevin Durant is the same way and Steph Curry. They haven't lost their love of competition. And what I like about players like Brady, like LeBron, and Michael Jordan came back late, but he went to a bad team in the Wizards. But do it until you can't. Because when you turn 50 and then you get to 60, you don't want to look back and say, shoot, you know what, I should have played a few more years.
quotes.social_post: Frank Isola on the longevity of stars like Steph Curry and LeBron James: They have not lost their love of competition. You should do it until you can't, because you don't want to look back and wish you played more.
